Create a 3D annotation layer

Source: R/annotate-3d.R
annotate_3d.Rd

annotate_3d() adds annotations to a plot: points, text labels, segments, polygons, axes, reference lines, or planes, at positions given as parameters rather than mapped from data. It works like ggplot2::annotate(), but builds a ggcube layer, which is depth-sorted together with the plot's other 3D layers, so annotations pass in front of and behind the plot's geometry correctly.

Usage

annotate_3d(type, ...)

Arguments

type

Character string specifying the annotation type. One of "point", "text", "segment", "polygon", "axes", "refline", or "plane".

...

Type-specific parameters, described below, along with parameters of the layer function the type uses, such as scale_depth, on_top, or light.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Details

Parameters can be vectors to create several annotations of the same type in one call, with values of length 1 recycled. Annotations never inherit the plot's aesthetics or appear in legends.

Each type builds a layer with a ggcube layer function, and takes that function's parameters:

Point annotations

Uses geom_point_3d(). Requires x, y, z. Optional styling: colour/color (default "black"), fill, size (default 2), shape (default 19), alpha, stroke.

Text annotations

Uses geom_text_3d(). Requires x, y, z, label. Optional styling: colour/color, size, alpha, family, fontface, hjust, vjust, angle, lineheight. Labels are depth-sorted with the rest of the scene, so geometry in front of a label hides it; use on_top = TRUE to draw labels on top of everything else instead, keeping them legible wherever they fall.

Segment annotations

Uses geom_segment_3d(). Requires x, y, z, xend, yend, zend. Optional styling: colour/color, linewidth, linetype, alpha, and arrow, an arrow specification created by grid::arrow(). Closed arrowheads are filled with the segment colour, unless arrow.fill is given. When a segment passes through a polygon and is split, its arrowheads stay at the segment's original ends.

Polygon annotations

Uses geom_polygon_3d(). Requires x, y, z giving the polygon's vertices in order. To draw several polygons in one call, give group, with one value per vertex; vertices sharing a value form one polygon. Each polygon needs at least 3 vertices. Optional styling: fill (default "grey50"), alpha (default 0.5), colour/color for the outline (default "grey30"), linewidth (default 0.5), linetype. Styling values apply per polygon, so they must have length 1 or one value per polygon, in the order the groups first appear.

Axes annotations

Uses geom_axes_3d(), which draws a line along each of the x, y, and z axes through an origin x, y, z (default 0), spanning the panel, with arrowheads and labels at their high ends. See geom_axes_3d() for its parameters.

Reference line annotations

Uses geom_refline_3d(), which draws infinite lines through the point x, y, z (default 0) in the direction dx, dy, dz, clipped to the panel. For example, the line spanned by a vector v is annotate_3d("refline", dx = v[1], dy = v[2], dz = v[3]), and the vertical line at x = 1, y = 2 is annotate_3d("refline", x = 1, y = 2, dz = 1).

Plane annotations

Uses geom_plane_3d(), which draws planes clipped to the panel, given as xintercept, yintercept, or zintercept; as intercept, slope_x, and slope_y; or as general coefficients a, b, c, d. See geom_plane_3d() for details.

Axes, reference lines, and planes are built from the panel's limits when the plot is drawn, so unlike the other types, they don't expand the plot's axis ranges.

Coordinates

Annotation coordinates are placed directly in the plot's (transformed) scale space: with scale_x_log10(), for example, give x positions as log10 values.

Coincident elements

A point, segment, line, or text label lying exactly in the plane of a polygon (such as a line drawn along a plane, or along the intersection of two planes) is drawn on top of that polygon.

Examples

p <- ggplot(mountain, aes(x, y, z)) +
  geom_surface_3d() +
  coord_3d(ratio = c(2, 3, 1),
           light = light(direction = c(-1, 0, 0)))

# A point, depth-sorted with the surface
p + annotate_3d("point", x = .5, y = .25, z = 100, color = "red", size = 3)


# Vectorized: several points in one call
p + annotate_3d("point", x = .5, y = .25, z = seq(50, 100, 5),
                color = "red", size = 3)


# Several annotation types
p +
  annotate_3d("segment", x = .5, y = .25, z = 100,
              xend = .5, yend = .25, zend = 50, color = "red") +
  annotate_3d("point", x = .5, y = .25, z = 100, color = "red", size = 3) +
  annotate_3d("text", x = .5, y = .25, z = 100, label = "Look here!",
              color = "red", vjust = -1, fontface = "bold", on_top = TRUE)


# Planes of a linear system, meeting at its solution, and the line along
# which the first two planes intersect
A <- rbind(c(1, 1, 1), c(1, -1, 0), c(0, 1, -1))
ggplot(data.frame(x = 1/3, y = 1/3, z = 1/3), aes(x, y, z)) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 3) +
  annotate_3d("plane", a = A[, 1], b = A[, 2], c = A[, 3], d = c(1, 0, 0),
              fill = c("tomato", "seagreen", "steelblue")) +
  annotate_3d("refline", x = 1/3, y = 1/3, z = 1/3,
              dx = 1, dy = 1, dz = -2, linewidth = 1) +
  lims(x = c(-1, 1), y = c(-1, 1)) + zlim(-1, 1) +
  coord_3d()


# A polygon: the triangle spanned by two vectors and the origin
u <- c(1, 0.2, 0.5); v <- c(0.3, 1, 0.8)
ggplot(data.frame(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, xend = c(u[1], v[1]),
                  yend = c(u[2], v[2]), zend = c(u[3], v[3])),
       aes(x, y, z, xend = xend, yend = yend, zend = zend)) +
  geom_segment_3d(arrow = arrow(type = "closed", length = unit(8, "pt"))) +
  annotate_3d("polygon", x = c(0, u[1], v[1]), y = c(0, u[2], v[2]),
              z = c(0, u[3], v[3]), fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_3d()


# Axes through the origin, depth-sorted with a surface
ggplot() +
  geom_function_3d(fun = function(x, y) (x^2 - y^2) / 2,
                   xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1), n = 20) +
  annotate_3d("axes", linewidth = 0.8) +
  coord_3d(panels = "none") +
  theme_void()
